class.name: Terrain3DStreamer
class.description: This class manages runtime region streaming. Regions around the clipmap target are loaded on background threads and evicted as the target moves away, so memory scales with the loaded area instead of the whole terrain. It works with the slot pool in [Terrain3DData]; see [method Terrain3DData.enable_streaming]. The loaded area is a keep set: the union of the clipmap target's own area ([member distance], scaled by [member camera_scale]) and any shapes added with [method add_keep_circle], [method add_keep_path] and [method add_keep_cone]. Regions inside the keep set load, regions outside it evict, with one region of hysteresis around the shapes. With no shapes the keep set is the clipmap target's area alone, as before. Shapes are in world units on the XZ plane. A region is inside a circle or a path corridor when any part of its footprint is within the radius; a cone is a half ellipse ahead of its origin and a smaller one behind it, grown by half a region, so it keeps every region it overlaps. Load order: regions behind the direction of travel last, then destination shapes, then paths in order of arrival (the part of the path ahead of the clipmap target, nearest first), then everything else nearest first. The direction of travel is the tangent of the first path at the clipmap target, else the direction of the first cone; without either nothing counts as behind. Only regions inside the region map window ([member Terrain3D.region_map_size]) can take a slot. The window recentres on the clipmap target when its retained area leaves it; along a path or cone it also slides ahead, keeping the retained area at the rear, as soon as regions needed now lie outside it, so the regions ahead take a slot with time to spare. A shape beyond the window, and a region the slot pool cannot hold yet, load their region bodies into a RAM cache ([member keep_cache_limit]) and they insert as soon as a slot is free and the window reaches them. If the pool has fewer slots than the keep set needs, the regions ahead of the direction of travel are kept first, the nearest first (a path by arrival), regions behind it last, and the rest are counted as [code skip-lint]deferred[/code] in [method get_stats]. For long camera flights see [method set_keep_path_ahead], [member behind_limit], [method get_path_ready_distance] and [method get_path_cost]. A flight keeps a path, a forward cone and (late) a destination circle, limits the path to a lookahead segment, sets [member behind_limit] to one region, and a game side governor limits the camera speed to what [method get_path_ready_distance] shows is visible. Preloading the destination only when time to arrival drops below the time it needs to load, and the rest of the corridor as cached bodies when memory allows, is up to the caller. Suspend dynamic collision during a long flight with [code skip-lint]collision_mode = Terrain3DCollision.DISABLED[/code] (set after the node is in the tree) and restore it at landing, or each landed region near the fast moving target triggers a collision refresh of about 25 ms. When a shape shrinks (a smaller radius, length or width, a shorter path) or is removed, or [member camera_scale] decreases, the next step evicts every region outside the new keep set at once, saving edited regions through the same worker thread as any eviction if [member persist_edits] is on (the early eviction is not limited by [member frame_budget_ms]), and drops loads still in flight for them. That keep set becomes the hysteresis baseline. Callers that want a gradual release lower the size a little each frame. Moving or growing a shape evicts nothing early. Settings are exposed as aliases on the [Terrain3D] node (e.g. [member Terrain3D.streaming_enabled]), which is also where they are saved. Streaming only runs outside the editor; the editor always keeps the full terrain loaded.

method.name: abort_pending
method.description: Consumes and drops every in flight threaded load. An unconsumed threaded load stays pinned in the ResourceLoader forever, so this runs whenever streaming stops: rescans, disabling streaming at runtime, and leaving the tree.

method.name: add_keep_circle
method.description: Keeps every region within [param radius] world units of [param center] loaded, ignoring the height. Returns an id for [method set_keep_circle] and [method remove_keep]. A [param destination] shape loads before every other shape, e.g. the landing area of a long camera jump.

method.name: add_keep_cone
method.description: Keeps a forward biased area loaded: a half ellipse reaching [param length] world units from [param origin] along [param direction] (its Y component is ignored) and [param half_width] to each side, plus a smaller half ellipse of depth [param behind] on the other side. The region around [param origin] is always kept. Use it for a camera that looks where it travels, with [member camera_scale] set to 0. Returns an id for [method set_keep_cone] and [method remove_keep].

method.name: add_keep_path
method.description: Keeps a corridor of [param radius] world units around the polyline through [param points] (at least two) loaded. Path regions load in order of arrival: nearest along the path first, starting from the point of the path closest to the clipmap target, regions behind that point last. Returns an id for [method set_keep_path] and [method remove_keep].

method.name: clear_keep
method.description: Removes every keep shape and resets [member camera_scale] to 1, restoring the default loaded area. Regions outside it evict at the next step.

method.name: clear_virtual_locations
method.description: Forgets every location added with [method register_virtual_locations] and rescans the data directory.

method.name: get_keep_count
method.description: The number of keep shapes added with the [code skip-lint]add_keep_*[/code] methods. The clipmap target's own area is not counted.

method.name: get_max_distance
method.description: The largest [member distance] the current [member slots] capacity and the region map window can hold with the current [member shape].

method.name: get_cached_regions
method.description: Returns the locations (Vector2i) whose region body waits in the RAM cache, for debug overlays and tests.

method.name: get_path_cost
method.description: Estimates what a corridor of [param radius] world units around a polyline costs to hold, so a caller can compare it with a memory budget before prefetching it. Returns [code skip-lint]length[/code] (meters along the polyline), [code skip-lint]cells[/code] (regions the corridor touches), [code skip-lint]regions[/code] (those with a file), [code skip-lint]region_bytes[/code] (the raw size of one region body: region_size squared times 4 bytes for each of height, control and, if [member Terrain3D.color_map_enabled] is on, color), [code skip-lint]bytes[/code] (regions times region_bytes, the RAM cache cost of holding every body) and [code skip-lint]outside_window[/code] (regions beyond the region map window now, which can only be cached until the window reaches them).

method.name: get_path_ready_distance
method.description: Returns the meters along the path [param id], from the clipmap target's position on it (or from [param from_distance] meters along the path if it is not negative), to the first region the path corridor needs that is not visible yet, or to the end of the path if all are. Only regions inserted into the region map count: a body waiting in the RAM cache or partway through a budgeted insertion is not visible. Regions behind the starting point, without a file, or given up on after repeated failures are skipped. Returns -1 for an unknown id. A game side camera governor uses it to never outrun the loaded terrain: the camera may only fly at a speed from which it can still stop inside the ready distance less a safety margin, [code skip-lint]speed_limit = sqrt(2 * brake * (ready_distance - safety))[/code], which gives [code skip-lint]ready_distance / lookahead_seconds[/code] at a steady flight. The distance is measured to the entry of the first missing region into the corridor, so a missing region is reported early by up to the corridor radius.

method.name: get_pending_regions
method.description: Returns the locations (Vector2i) with a threaded load in flight, for debug overlays and tests that record the order of requests.

method.name: get_required_slots
method.description: How many pool slots the given distance needs with the current [member shape], including the one region hysteresis band. Square: (2 * (distance + 1) + 1)².

method.name: get_wanted_regions
method.description: Returns the locations (Vector2i) the last step wanted, which is what the streamer really uses: the regions needed now, or with [param cache_only] the regions that are only fetched as bodies into the RAM cache, ahead of the reach of a path (see [method set_keep_path_ahead]). A region is missing when it is wanted and [method Terrain3DData.has_region] is false. The [code skip-lint]wanted[/code] and [code skip-lint]missing[/code] stats count the first list only.

method.name: get_stats
method.description: Returns live streaming counters: [code skip-lint]streaming_active[/code], [code skip-lint]resident[/code], [code skip-lint]free_slots[/code], [code skip-lint]inflight[/code], [code skip-lint]staged[/code] (regions partway through a budgeted insertion), [code skip-lint]saving[/code] (evicted regions being written to disk), [code skip-lint]failed[/code] (locations whose load failed; each is requested again every few seconds, then ignored after three failures until [method scan_directory]), [code skip-lint]known[/code], [code skip-lint]landed_total[/code], [code skip-lint]evicted_total[/code], and [code skip-lint]land_ms_avg[/code] (an exponential moving average of an insertion's main thread cost in ms), and for the keep set [code skip-lint]keep_shapes[/code], [code skip-lint]wanted[/code] (known regions inside it), [code skip-lint]missing[/code] (wanted, inside the region map window, not resident yet), [code skip-lint]deferred[/code] (wanted but the slot pool cannot hold them) [code skip-lint]outside_window[/code] (wanted but beyond the region map window, waiting in the RAM cache), [code skip-lint]nearest_missing[/code] (meters from the clipmap target to the nearest wanted region that is not visible yet and not behind the direction of travel, -1 if none), [code skip-lint]recentres[/code] (region map window moves so far) and [code skip-lint]collision_refreshes[/code] (dynamic collision refreshes the streamer asked for). Useful for debug overlays and tests.

method.name: is_active
method.description: Returns [code skip-lint]true[/code] when streaming is enabled and the game is running outside the editor.

method.name: register_virtual_locations
method.description: Makes locations known to the streamer that have no file in the data directory, so a [member resolver] can supply them. They stream like any other location. A virtual location the resolver does not answer for is looked up as the normal file name, fails to load and is marked failed. Registered locations survive [method scan_directory].

method.name: remove_keep
method.description: Removes a keep shape. Regions only it kept evict at the next step, without hysteresis. Unknown ids are ignored.

method.name: scan_directory
method.description: Scans the data directory for region locations and resets streaming state. Only file names are read, nothing is loaded. Called automatically at initialization while streaming is active.

method.name: set_keep_circle
method.description: Moves or resizes a circle in place. Returns [code skip-lint]false[/code] if [param id] is not a circle. A smaller radius evicts early; see the class description.

method.name: set_keep_cone
method.description: Moves, turns or resizes a cone in place, e.g. every frame with the camera. Returns [code skip-lint]false[/code] if [param id] is not a cone. A zero [param direction] keeps the old one. A smaller length, half width or behind evicts early; see the class description.

method.name: set_keep_path_ahead
method.description: Limits a path to the stretch the camera needs. Regions further than [param ahead] world units along the path from the clipmap target's position on it are not wanted: they take no slot, no load order and are not in the [code skip-lint]wanted[/code] and [code skip-lint]missing[/code] stats, so regions behind a moving camera release as it passes. A negative [param ahead] restores the whole path. [param prefetch] reaches further, for region bodies only: the regions up to that many world units ahead (negative: to the end of the path) load into the RAM cache ([member keep_cache_limit]) without taking a slot, and insert when they become needed. They are requested after everything that is needed, and never use the last of [member concurrent_loads] while a needed region is waiting; a needed body that does not fit in the cache takes the place of the farthest prefetched one. A caller that knows the memory is there (see [method get_path_cost]) prefetches the whole corridor this way without delaying the near path. Returns [code skip-lint]false[/code] if [param id] is not a path.

method.name: set_keep_path
method.description: Replaces a path's points and radius in place, e.g. to drop the part behind the camera. Returns [code skip-lint]false[/code] if [param id] is not a path. A smaller radius or fewer points evicts early; see the class description.

method.name: step
method.description: Runs the streaming state machine once: evicts regions that fell outside the loaded area, inserts completed loads, and requests missing regions. Called automatically once per physics frame while streaming is active.

members.member: Keeps nothing further than this many world units behind the clipmap target, against the direction of travel (see the class description). A region whose center is more than the limit plus half a region behind is neither loaded nor retained, whichever shape or area would keep it, with no hysteresis: with a limit of one region size, the region the target stands in, the next one ahead and the one behind it stay, and everything further behind unloads, through the worker thread (and its save if [member persist_edits] is on). Destination shapes are exempt. A negative value turns it off. Setting it, or lowering it, evicts at once. It needs a path or a cone to define the direction of travel. For a cone alone, [code skip-lint]behind = region_size[/code] and [member camera_scale] 0 hold one region behind the target; the limit is what trims a path.

Scales the clipmap target's own loaded area: [member distance] x camera_scale regions. 1 is the normal area, 0 removes it so that only keep shapes load. Lowering it evicts the area it gave up at once, with no hysteresis band. To shrink gradually, lower it a little every frame. [method clear_keep] resets it to 1.
How many regions may be loading on background threads at once. Loading runs wide while insertions stay narrow; see [member loads_per_frame].

How far the loaded area extends from the clipmap target, in regions. For example, 4 with a square [member shape] keeps a 9x9 block of regions loaded (the target region plus 4 in every direction); a circle of the same radius keeps fewer. In world units the radius is distance x region_size x vertex_spacing. Higher values load more of the world at once and cost more memory. Raising distance automatically raises [member slots] to fit, so it just works; lowering slots below what the current distance needs pulls distance back down (with a warning). The maximum is bounded by the 1024 slot ceiling (square shape tops out at distance 14) and by the region map window, which must hold distance + 1 regions on each side of the target: (size - 3) / 2, or 14 for the default 32. See [member Terrain3D.region_map_size]. The window recentres on the target whenever the loaded area would leave it, so streamed region locations are not limited.

Enables region streaming at runtime. Instead of loading every region up front, regions within [member distance] of the clipmap target are loaded on background threads and evicted as the target moves away. Streaming is a read-only view of the data directory: eviction drops a region together with any runtime edits unless [member persist_edits] is on. Has no effect inside the editor; see [method is_active].

Main thread time, in milliseconds, that region insertions and evictions may take per physics frame. Uploading a region's texture layers is the main cost of streaming and grows with [member Terrain3D.region_size], so an insertion is split into steps (height map, control map, color map, then making the region visible). Steps run until the budget is spent, and at least one runs every frame, so the cost of a frame is about the budget plus one step instead of the whole region. Small regions complete several per frame; large regions are spread over a few frames. A region becomes visible only after all of its steps are done. The same budget spreads building the region's [Terrain3DInstancer] instances over frames, one mesh asset at a time. Lower values keep frame times steadier but fill the loaded area more slowly. Raise it, or set it to 0 (each region is then inserted at once, up to [member loads_per_frame] per frame), while a loading screen hides the hitch, for example after a teleport. Alias target of [member Terrain3D.streaming_frame_budget_ms].

The most region bodies kept in the RAM cache for keep shapes beyond the region map window while [member mode] is DISK. Each cached region costs its full raw size (about 3 MB at 512 m with all maps). RAM mode caches everything anyway. Prefetching a whole corridor (see [method set_keep_path_ahead]) needs a limit of at least the number of its regions beyond the window and the pool, [code skip-lint]outside_window[/code] from [method get_path_cost] and more.

What eviction does with a region's data. DISK drops the region; RAM keeps every body cached in memory (and prefetches the rest of the world in the background with spare load budget), so only the GPU layers follow the loaded area and revisits never touch the disk. RAM mode trades memory for the smoothest possible region changes. In either mode a region's edits are written back only when [member persist_edits] is on. Alias target of [member Terrain3D.streaming_mode].

How many completed region loads may be inserted into the terrain per physics frame. Each insertion uploads texture layers and updates collision on the main thread, so raising this trades hitching for faster fill in. Only used when [member frame_budget_ms] is 0, which replaces it with a time budget.

Whether a region modified at runtime is written back to the data directory when it is evicted (and, in RAM mode, when the cache is flushed by leaving RAM mode or disabling streaming). The write happens on a worker thread, so it does not stall the frame; the region is not reloaded until its file is complete. Off by default: streaming is a read-only view of the data on disk, so eviction drops the region together with its runtime edits and a revisit reloads the on-disk version. In RAM mode the edits survive eviction in the cache until it is flushed. Turn it on for a world that should persist runtime edits; otherwise save explicitly with [method Terrain3DData.save_directory]. Note that persisting can overwrite an edit made to the same region file by another process while the region was resident. Alias target of [member Terrain3D.streaming_persist_edits].

Optional hook that lets several locations share one region file (a tile library with reuse). Signature: [code skip-lint]func(location: Vector2i) -> Dictionary[/code]. Return [code skip-lint]{"path": String, "rotation": int, "mirror": bool, "read_only": bool}[/code]; only [code skip-lint]path[/code] is required. [code skip-lint]rotation[/code] is 0-3 clockwise quarter turns, applied after [code skip-lint]mirror[/code] (a flip of the x axis). They are applied to the height, control and color maps; control map pixels move whole, so the packed texture ids stay exact. The loaded region is placed at the requested location, not the file's own. An empty Dictionary or an empty [code skip-lint]path[/code] means the normal file for the location, so with no resolver nothing changes. The resolver is called on the main thread each time the streamer requests a location, never on a loader thread: keep it fast, such as a Dictionary lookup. The mirror and rotation also run on the main thread, right before insertion, because ResourceLoader's threaded load has no hook for loader thread code. Locations that share a file load one at a time. [code skip-lint]read_only[/code] regions are never written to disk: [member persist_edits] skips them, [method Terrain3DRegion.save] refuses them. Their modified flag may still be set; it is ignored. A runtime edit to one is kept while the region stays resident and is discarded on eviction (in RAM mode, while the body stays cached); the shared file is never changed. Promoting an edited reused region to a file of its own is not implemented. Use [method register_virtual_locations] for locations without a file.
The shape of the loaded area around the clipmap target: a square block or a circle of radius [member distance]. A circle loads ~21% fewer regions at the same distance.

Capacity of the pooled texture arrays, in regions. Sized automatically when you raise [member distance] (the pool must hold every region within distance + 1 for hysteresis: (2 * (distance + 1) + 1)² for a square shape, so 25 at distance 1, 121 at distance 4). Set it directly only to reserve extra headroom; setting it below what the current distance needs clamps distance down. Changing it while streaming rebuilds the terrain data at the new capacity.

constants.constant: The loaded area is a square block of regions around the clipmap target.
The loaded area is a circle of regions around the clipmap target.
Evicted regions save (if modified) and drop; RAM and GPU both follow the loaded area.
Region bodies stay cached in RAM; only the GPU layers follow the loaded area.
